title: Etale equivalence relations have algebraic-space quotients
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $V$ a scheme over $S$. Let $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism of schemes such that for every $S$-scheme $T$ the image of $R(T)$ in $V(T)\times V(T)$ is an equivalence relation, and assume $s$ and $t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], for the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], of the presheaf $T\mapsto V(T)/R(T)$. Then $F$ is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], $q:h_V\to F$ is etale and surjective, and the map $h_R\to h_V\times_Fh_V$ induced by $(s,t)$ is an isomorphism. In particular, every section of $F$ over a scheme lifts to $V$ on an etale covering. For any fppf sheaf $G$, composition with $q$ is a bijection between maps $F\to G$ and maps $h_V\to G$ whose composites with $s,t$ agree.

source.place: Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation); Tag 02WV (lemma-when-it-works-it-works), with the presentation kernel-pair identity and the defining sheaf quotient universal property.

proof.text: The kernel-pair assertion of [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] makes the presheaf quotient unit injective: lift two classes to representatives, lift their equal images to R, and use the coequalizer equation. The injection of restricted quotient presheaves from [lem-trf-etale-pullback-relation-presheaf] therefore embeds each restricted quotient into F. Apply Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify to its range inside F. Subfunctor.sheafifyLift and to_sheafify_lift_unique prove the sheafification universal property. Thus the intermediate quotient sheaves exist in the original value universe, with no global sheafification instance.

Apply [lem-trf-etale-quotient-affine-open-cover] to V.affineCover and the quotient sheaves constructed in step 1. Its restricted chart relations are monomorphic etale equivalence relations. For each affine chart, [lem-trf-etale-affine-quotient-representable] gives the diagonal and quotient-map representability; [lem-trf-representable-etale-quotient-presentation] makes the chart map surjective etale. Hence each chart quotient is an algebraic space by [def-trf-algebraic-space].

Use the existence clause of [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] to form the coproduct H of chart quotient sheaves. The coproduct of their scheme atlases is the explicit coproduct from step 2, so [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct] makes H algebraic. Each chart inclusion in F is representable open and hence mono: base change along a section and use monicity of the representing open scheme map. The local lifting clause of step 2 makes H to F locally surjective, hence epi by sheaf separation. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-space-open-gluing].

Representability of the diagonal implies representability of the quotient map by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [def-pc-fibre-product]: for scheme tests T and V, pull the diagonal back along their pair on T times_S V. Its representing scheme has projections to T and V; the two pullback universal properties identify its sections with pairs having equal F image. Apply [lem-trf-representable-etale-quotient-presentation] to obtain etaleness and surjectivity of every scheme test and an etale covering family lifting each section. Its generated sieve is covering in the over-topology and naturality extends the lifts to its arrows. The square is [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair].
An equalizing map descends along the presheaf coequalizer. Surjectivity of the hom-set map in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends this to F; injectivity and coequalizer hom_ext give uniqueness.

lean.statement: theorem etale_relation_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} {R V : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (hη : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun g : F.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ g)) : IsAlgebraicSpace F ∧ IsEtale (relationQuotientMap s t F η) ∧ IsSurjective (relationQuotientMap s t F η) ∧ IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) (relationQuotientMap s t F η) (relationQuotientMap s t F η) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (x : F.obj.obj (op T)), ∃ C : Sieve T, C ∈ (Scheme.etaleTopology.over S) T ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (f : U ⟶ T), C f → ∃ a : U ⟶ V, (relationQuotientMap s t F η).app (op U) a = F.obj.map f.op x) ∧ (∀ (G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (f : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G.obj), yoneda.map s ≫ f = yoneda.map t ≫ f → ∃! g : F.obj ⟶ G.obj, relationQuotientMap s t F η ≫ g = f)
lean.note: The quotient presheaf is the coequalizer of the Yoneda maps. F and its unit η are specified by the sheafification universal property at this presheaf; no global HasWeakSheafify assumption is imposed on the big site. IsPullback expresses that the canonical relation-to-kernel-pair map is an isomorphism. The final unique-factorization clause is the stated bijection on equalizing maps.
